questions.question: Which of the following instruments is normally played in a vertical position and with an arched bow?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sarangi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**Sarangi**

__
 
• It is also called **saran **or **Saranga**, short-necked fiddle used throughout South Asia, particularly for folk and classical Hindustani music. Measuring about 76 cm (30 inches) long, the instrument has a roughly rectangular slightly waisted body and broad fretless neck generally carved from a single piece of wood.
 
• It has three melody strings made of gut, usually tuned a fifth and a fourth apart, and 11 to 37 sympathetically vibrating metal strings.
 
• **The musician, who is seated, normally holds the instrument against his left shoulder in a vertical position and plays with an arched bow held in an underhand grip in his right hand. Hence, Option 4 is correct.**
 
• The cuticles (or sometimes the space on the fingernail just above the cuticles) of the left hand are pressed against the strings to sound specific pitches.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a96a6d6b9106400bfc249da27121877dc089d6af73e6eb6d9a6708ee955316c7.png] ​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Shehnai**

 
• **It is double-reed conical oboe of North India**.
 
• The Shehnai is made of wood, except for a flaring metal bell attached to the bottom of the instrument, and measures about 12–20 inches (30–50 cm) in length, with six to eight keyless finger holes along its body.

**Veena**

 
• **It is among the oldest Indian musical instruments.**
 
• From the references to Vedic writings, it can date back to around the first millennium B.C. Temple sculptures from the 2nd century B.C. show a type of veena being played.
 
• The Saraswati Veena is predominant in Carnatic music and the Rudra veena is the most played veena in Hindustani music.
 
• The Saraswati veena has seven strings strung over twenty-four fixed frets.
 
• It is played by sitting cross-legged, with the resonator to the player's right.
 
• The veena is said to be the** only instrument that can play all the Gamakas **(oscillations) in Carnatic music, usually something that only the most proficient vocalists can achieve.
 
• The Hindu Goddess of Knowledge, Saraswati, is said to play the Veena.
 
• Pictures depict her sitting on a lotus and playing the instrument.

**Sitar**

 
• **It is a **stringed instrument of the lute family that is popular in northern **India, Pakistan, **and **Bangladesh**.
 
• The instrument was invented in medieval India, flourished in the 16th and 17th centuries, and arrived at its present form in 18th-century India.
 
• Used widely throughout the Indian subcontinent, the sitar became popularly known in the wider world through the works of **Ravi Shankar**, beginning in the late 1950s and early 1960s.

• It is said to most resemble the sound of the human voice, able to imitate vocal ornaments such as gamaks (shakes) and meends (sliding movements).
 
• The Sarangi is typically played while sitting cross-legged, with the instrument held vertically in front of the player.
 
• The instrument is played with a bow, and the main strings are stopped with the cuticles or nails of the left hand, while the other fingers are used to modulate the pitch and resonance.

• It is known for its deep, weighty, introspective sound and is used both for solo performances and as an accompaniment.
 
• The Sarod is played with a plectrum, and the strings are stopped with the nails of the left hand.

questions.question: Which of the following is a cyclic arrangement of time units in Hindustani classical music?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tala**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tala** is the term used in Hindustani classical music to denote a cyclic arrangement of time units.
 
• It serves as a rhythmic framework for the performance and is essential for the structuring of the music.
 
• Each tala is characterized by a specific number of beats, known as **matras**, which are grouped into sections called **vibhags**.
 
• Common talas in Hindustani music include **Teentaal, Ektaal, and Jhaptaal**.
 
• The tala system is crucial for both the composition and improvisation in performances, guiding the timing and rhythm.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Hindustani classical music, one of the two main sub-genres of Indian classical music, has a rich tradition and history dating back to the Vedic times.
 
• It is characterized by a wide variety of **ragas (melodic frameworks)** and **talas (rhythmic cycles)**, each with specific rules and structures.
 
• Unlike Western classical music, Hindustani music places a significant emphasis on improvisation within the set frameworks of raga and tala.
 
• The performance of a piece in Hindustani classical music often involves a gradual development from slow, meditative sections to fast, intricate passages.
 
• This genre of music has been influenced by various cultural and historical factors, including Persian and Mughal traditions.
